questions.q: Identify the sentence with the grammatical error.
o: She has been living here since five years.
He is fond of playing football with his friends.
They have gone to the market to buy some vegetables.
The committee consists of ten members.
questions.x: 'Since' should be followed by a duration (e.g., 'since five years ago') or a point in time, not just a duration alone.

questions.q: Spot the error in the sentence.
o: Each of the boys have completed their homework.
Neither of the twins is ready to leave.
The news about the accident were shocking.
The team is playing well; they have won all matches.
questions.x: 'Each' is singular, so the verb should be 'has' instead of 'have'.

o: The keys to success lies in hard work and perseverance.
The data collected from the survey is inconclusive.
The scissors are kept on the table.
The police have arrested the thief.
questions.x: 'Keys' is plural, so the correct verb should be 'lie' (plural form).
'Exodus' refers to a mass departure; 'influx' means an arrival or incoming.
'Voracious' means having a huge appetite; 'indifferent' means lacking interest or enthusiasm.
'Transient' means lasting only a short time; 'permanent' means lasting indefinitely.
'Laudable' means deserving praise; 'blameworthy' means deserving blame.
'Ostentatious' means intended to attract notice; 'modest' means unassuming.
'Reticent' means not revealing one's thoughts; 'talkative' means tending to talk a lot.
